You are given exactly two pixel-aligned images of the same shelf scene.

Image 1 is a numbered RGB image. Each red numbered marker identifies one physical object.

Image 2 is a grayscale metric depth map rendered from the same camera at the same resolution.
Brighter pixels represent surfaces closer to the camera.
Darker pixels represent surfaces farther from the camera.
This brightness convention and depth normalization are fixed across all scenes.

The same red numbered markers are overlaid at exactly the same pixel coordinates in Image 1 and Image 2.
The same ID in both images identifies the same physical object.
Use these repeated markers only to establish object correspondence between the two images.
The marker color, marker size, and marker pixels contain no depth information.
Determine depth from the grayscale of the visible physical body surrounding each marker in Image 2.

The following IDs are confirmed to be the complete and correct set of visible object-marker IDs:
[58, 74, 88]

Use Image 1 to identify each numbered object and Image 2 at the corresponding image position to determine its depth.

List all confirmed IDs from the physical object closest to the camera to the physical object farthest from the camera.

In visible_ids, return the provided ID list in its original order.
In front_to_back, return the same IDs ordered from closest to farthest.

Return only one valid JSON object:

{
  "visible_ids": [],
  "front_to_back": []
}
